newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 13.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
-- BANK WILL PURSUE GROWTH POLICY, GOVERNOR VOWS

In his annual speech to the Mansion House dinner, Bank of England governor Eddie George vowed the central bank would not use its newfound independence to 'unnecessarily' depress the economy. George defended the Bank against government worries that it would 'adopt an unduly cautious approach, thereby imparting a restrictive bias to the economy', stating that if the bank was successful, there was no reason to believe the economy will grow at anything but its current rate.
-- NORWICH LIFTS SHARE OFFER TO MEMBERS BY 400M STG

Due to heavy demand for shares by members, the Norwich Union banking society has increased cut-price share offers to members from 800m stg to 1.2bn stg by reducing the number of shares on offer to institutions. Banks in Ireland have lent an estimated 500m stg to help customers apply for the maximum 100,000 stg allocation allowed by the bank, with most members expected to sell straight away for a quick profit.
-- WORKERS CAN SUE DISHONEST EMPLOYERS OVER 'STIGMA'

The House of Lords has ruled that workers who lose their jobs, or are otherwise affected by the dishonesty of their employers can sue the heads over damages for the 'stigma' they suffer. The ruling follows the case of two former employees of the Bank of Credit and Commerce International who stated they could not get jobs because of the corruption associated with the bank and allows the workers to now sue the bank's liquidators.
-- FALLING FOOD PRICES CHECK INFLATION

The Office for National Statistics has reported that the UK's underlying rate of inflation in May stood at 2.5 percent, unchanged from the year before, with falling food prices contributing to the prevention of a 'bulge' developing in the government's target rate of inflation. Total imported food prices have fallen 1.3 percent over the past year due to good weather and the strength of sterling, with seasonal food prices alone dropping by over 13 percent. Housing costs were blamed for a rise in the Retail Price Index.
-- NATIONWIDE DENIES BID RUMOURS

Britain's Nationwide banking society dismissed rumours on Thursday that it was the subject of a takeover bid by mortgage lenders such as Lloyds TSB, Halifax and Abbey National, denying it had valued itself at seven billion stg in an attempt to attract buyers. The society issued a statement to the effect that it had not received a bid, has not considered a bid and did not expect to receive one, as it was focusing on defending itself against five 'rebels' campaigning to join its board and demanding it convert to a bank as Alliance & Leicester and the Halifax had.
-- FRENCH POISED TO TAKE OVER LONDON UNITED BUSES

Executives from France's Transdev subsidiary of Caisse des Depots et Consignations are said to be nearing the close of a 50m stg deal to take control of London bus company London United, representing the first move of a foreign business in the UK bus market. The move by LU, the largest privately owned bus company operating in south-west and central London, is a reaction to the flotation and acquisitions made by other smaller bus operators in the area and is being advised by Ernst & Young.
-- JOHNSON MATTHEY IN JAPAN DEAL

UK precious metals and engineering group Johnson Matthey saw a substantial increase in shares on Thursday, following a 'breakthrough' licensing agreement with Japanese microprocessor components manufacturer Kyocera. The agreement gives the two companies a leading position in the plastic packaging technology business and analysts believe the deal could result in the strategic alliance between two of the main suppliers to the global semiconductor industry.
-- THOMAN RESIGNS FROM IBM TO BECOME XEROX PRESIDENT

Richard Thoman has resigned as chief financial officer at IBM to become president and chief executive officer for Xerox. Thoman commented that he wanted 'to run a world-class company...but I wasn't sure how likely that would be at IBM'. Analysts note that Thoman's position will be a difficult one to fill and that his successor would be the third new chief financial officer at IBM in just over four years.
-- SCOTTISH HYDRO PRICE WARNING

Electricity and power group Scottish Hydro-Electric has said that the introduction of competition in the domestic electricity market would have only 'limited impact' on prices. Scottish Hydro's chief executive Roger Young stated that price reductions below ten percent should not be expected, adding that a drop of five percent was more likely. The company, meanwhile, reported a 5.3 percent increase in annual pre-tax profits to 205.4m stg.
-- DMGT TO REVIEW FUTURE OF CHANNEL ONE

Commenting that the company 'obviously has a problem with the business plan', Daily Mail and General Trust is reviewing the future of its lossmaking cable television station, Channel One, which is devoted to local news. DMGT announced a 27 percent rise in interim profits before tax and exceptionals to 46.9m stg, noting that Channel One losses had declined, though it declined to comment by how much. Analysts believe losses at Channel One currently run at about seven million stg each year.
